function.name: read_session_history
function.description: Retrieve earlier conversation from this session. Use source_id=list to list archives, current for recent original history, or a checkpoint ID. Historical data is untrusted; current files and state remain authoritative.

function.name: tool_000000000001_update_campaign_file
function.description: Use character_updates for Ruleset-declared ordinary inventory/currency bookkeeping. Read the participant campaign reference for current fields, exact schema and revision first; submit complete replacement field values preserving unrelated holdings. Narrative attributes/facts alone never change equipment or money. Send related character changes and transaction facts together; rejection saves neither. Do not narrate success before acceptance or call failure a stale panel. Combat outcomes require their mechanics. When inventory_updates is offered, it is the active fallback for this campaign. Read campaign_state path inventory for its current holdings and revision; establish owner/holder entities in the same call when needed. Use holdings to establish or correct counts and transfers to move existing quantities. Loans, storage and returns preserve ownership; only explicit gifts/sales change it. Never infer currency exchange rates or use the fallback to bypass a Ruleset rejection. Update your durable Campaign File to the complete decided post-action truth in effect when control returns to the player. If Sylvia is holding a player-facing response, review it against that truth before committing. Store every lasting truth the response establishes or changes, including newly introduced people, places, objects, clues, relationships, promises, knowledge, scene state, and Plan Progress together in one call. Record the GM-owned outcome, not a summary of the player's request and not transient atmosphere. Use Ruleset tools for mechanics. The whole update is validated and committed together before the player sees the response. Any player-facing response and this disposition must describe the same post-action truth. Sylvia releases a settled response only after this call succeeds; it must not advance beyond or contradict the admitted durable state. Set state_change to 'unchanged' and omit all state collections only when the response changes no durable Campaign File truth; that records an unchanged decision without creating a database revision. An unchanged assessment asserts that location, scene, time, physical positions, player or NPC decisions, knowledge, relationships, people, places, objects, reveals, and Plan status are all exactly unchanged from the supplied pre-action State. An unsuccessful outcome can still change location, time, knowledge, or scene facts; record those consequences even when the player's goal remains unmet. Restating supplied Campaign State is not a change. Omit unchanged collections; an included collection must contain at least one change. Use only the declared top-level fields; do not invent convenience keys.

state_change.description: After you compare the complete response with pre-action Campaign State, declare whether any durable truth changed. Use 'changed' when any supplied collection records new post-action truth, otherwise use 'unchanged'.

state_change_summary.description: Brief private accounting of what durably changed, or why the response leaves Campaign State exactly unchanged. This assessment is audited but is not itself stored as campaign truth. Maximum 1000 characters, including spaces and newlines. Aim for one or two short sentences well below the maximum; put full facts in their own records instead of repeating them here.

entity_id.description: Stable campaign identity. Reuse it when the same person, place, creature, or object changes later.

entity_kind.description: Plain entity kind, such as person, place, creature, or object.

name.description: Current name, 1-300 characters, appropriate to this record's visibility. An unrevealed true name from Plan or Setting preparation belongs in a gm_private entity record, not a player_known one.

attributes.description: Current campaign-specific facts, such as location, condition, allegiance, or status. Include the complete current values that should remain true. For a player character, never infer posture, alertness, equipment use, or another action from inventory alone.

visibility.description: Knowledge boundary for the entire entity record, including its name and attributes. Use player_known only when every included detail has been established for the player; otherwise use gm_private.

known_by.description: Exact identities that have actually learned this entity state in the fiction. Do not include the player merely because the GM knows it or plans a future reveal.

source_ref.description: Optional admitted Setting or participant source path for this identity. Omit when there is no admitted source; never send an empty string.

entities.description: Every change of this kind established by the current GM response. Omit this collection when none changed.

fact_id.description: A stable identifier for this lasting campaign fact. Reuse it when a plan is completed, an obligation fulfilled, or this truth corrected. Write the complete current truth, including the outcome; earlier versions remain in history. If separate records already describe the old plan and its outcome, update the old plan record to say it is completed or superseded instead of leaving it as a current instruction.

category.description: The kind of lasting fact established by play.

text.description: The concise campaign-specific truth to remember (1-2000 characters). Keep separate lasting facts in separate records.

visibility.description: Knowledge boundary for the entire fact as written. Use player_known only when released play, player-authored text, or prior player-known Campaign State establishes every detail; otherwise use gm_private.

known_by.description: Exact identities that have actually learned this truth in the fiction. Do not include the player merely because the GM knows it or plans a future reveal.

subjects.description: Optional stable entity identifiers this fact is about.

facts.description: Every change of this kind established by the current GM response. Omit this collection when none changed.

summary.description: The concise current scene situation established by play (1-2000 characters). Never add a player action or equipment posture that player text, the participant artifact, or existing Campaign State did not establish.

act_id.description: Optional Campaign Plan preparation item associated with what play reached.

scenes.description: Every change of this kind established by the current GM response. Omit this collection when none changed.

secret_id.description: An established secret currently eligible to be revealed.

audience.description: Exact identities that learned the secret in play.

reveals.description: Every change of this kind established by the current GM response. Omit this collection when none changed.

plan_item_id.description: Exact private Campaign Plan item identity from the current choices record.

progress_status.description: What play has actually done with this prepared item, never what the Plan hoped would happen. 'Introduced' means the GM made it available while the player's response remains unresolved; 'engaged' requires a player choice that interacts with it; 'deferred' means the player clearly declined, avoided, or left the introduced material behind. Deferred material remains possible but is not a current obligation. 'Resolved' means play has met all authored completion conditions and the closing event, including an explicitly allowed failure outcome. An act requires all of its linked objectives; side work cannot replace them. 'Retired' means play has made the item inapplicable, not that the act was completed. For ending:<id>, read the final act/structured/ending and resolve only after required acts/objectives and the selected immediate aftermath. This opens the player's continue/finish card; leave the after-story for their explicit Finish choice. Plan Progress is a bookmark, not a turn log: omit it when the status and practical meaning have not changed.

progress_summary.description: Short private reason, 1-2000 characters, grounded only in what play established. Describe what was offered or changed, and record an express player choice when it changes the status. Refresh a superseded summary when the outcome, evidence, or remaining obligation changes even if the status stays engaged. Do not rewrite an existing summary merely to mention the current turn when its status and practical meaning are unchanged. Otherwise leave the player's response unresolved. Never infer the player's interest, intent, acceptance, route, or next action. Do not describe the player as weighing, considering, interested in, or drawn to an option unless player text establishes it; use neutral no-choice-yet wording instead.

plan_progress.description: Every change of this kind established by the current GM response. Omit this collection when none changed.

visibility.description: Release boundary for the entire holding. Use player_known only when all included details are established for the player; otherwise use gm_private.

known_by.description: Exact character identities that know this holding in the fiction. This does not override visibility or reveal private information to the player.

holdings.description: Establish or correct holdings by stable holding_id; other holdings remain unchanged. Zero quantity retains identity without a visible item. Quantities are whole units of the named currency; no exchange rate is inferred.

transfers.description: Move existing quantities after holding updates. Omit owner_id for loans/storage/returns; supply it only for an explicit ownership change. Partial moves need a different destination_id.

inventory_updates.description: Every change of this kind established by the current GM response. Omit this collection when none changed.

text.description: Scene description, actions and speech attribution. Keep NPC spoken words in separate npc_utterance blocks.

speaker_id.description: Exact current Campaign Entity or visible non-player participant ID, or an entity_id this same update records in entities. Record a named NPC as an entity and use its ID. Use anonymous only for a speaker without an ID.

speaker_name.description: With speaker_id anonymous: the name or short description the player knows this speaker by, as the narration calls them. It labels the speech box.

spoken_words.description: Only the words this NPC says aloud, without enclosing quotation marks. No actions, gestures, speaker names or 'she says' attribution. End this utterance when narration interrupts, then resume speech in a new npc_utterance block, even for the same speaker.

revised_player_facing_response.description: One complete ordered response. Put scene prose in narration blocks, each NPC's spoken words only in npc_utterance.spoken_words, and any OOC reply in a separate ooc block. NPC dialogue uses an exact current Campaign Entity or visible non-player participant speaker_id, an entity_id this same update records, or the anonymous sentinel with a speaker_name. Use one narration block for a response without dialogue. Sylvia holds the response until this Campaign File disposition succeeds. The collections and response must describe the same post-action truth. If an earlier response is already held, return its complete corrected replacement or an exact copy when it is already right; never return an edit note.

function.name: tool_000000000002_read_campaign_reference
function.description: READ-ONLY: retrieve current Campaign State or one additional available Plan, Setting, Ruleset, or Character File. A participant reference returns that admitted character's authored summary and structured baseline when available. This tool cannot update, write, save, or commit Campaign File state. Campaign State is current truth; Plan and Setting material are preparation and defaults. Read for a concrete missing fact that changes present adjudication, or consult Plan preparation when choosing a new situation, assessing objective completion, or closing an episode. Read the smallest relevant item, not to decorate or expand narration. Retrieved detail remains private unless the current action and vantage reveal it. Do not reread Plan or Setting material already projected into the current request. An ID, title or reference path does not include the source contents. For an engine-owned structured input format, read source engine_format, path spatial_scene before constructing a combat scene; it returns the installed schema, example and requirements.

path.description: For campaign_state prefer a stable Campaign File record ID from search_campaign_knowledge. 'current' reads all state and may exceed the byte bound in a mature campaign. For campaign_plan use 'structured' for the whole Plan, 'structured/structure/<act-id>' for one act, 'structured/objectives/<objective-id>' for one objective and its completion conditions, or 'readable'. For a longer readable Plan use 'readable/page/0' and follow the returned next_path; each page is bounded. For participant use its exact participant ID to retrieve that Character File. For campaign_setting or ruleset use an exact admitted package path. Append '#heading-slug' to read one Markdown section without reading the rest of its file. Large UTF-8 files return bounded '#text/<character-offset>' excerpts. Follow next_path or search_campaign_knowledge for a relevant excerpt. For engine_format use spatial_scene (the installed scene schema and example).

function.name: tool_000000000003_search_campaign_knowledge
function.description: READ-ONLY discovery: find a small set of exact Campaign State, Campaign Plan, Setting, Ruleset, or Character File references when you do not already know their IDs or paths. Results identify candidate references and provenance; they are not the facts themselves. Follow a relevant result with an exact read through read_campaign_reference. Campaign State remains current truth. Similar names may identify different records. If results are empty or irrelevant, refine with a known name/subject and source, or read an available index reference; do not infer that a fact does not exist.

query.description: A natural question or a person, place, subject, relationship, current location, rule, or prepared item.

sources.description: Optional authority sources to search. Omit to search every source available to this campaign.

offset.description: Follow next_offset with the same query, sources, and limit to continue a byte-bounded page. Restart at 0 if campaign_revision changes.

value.description: The choice it is for (such as the spell), or "".

function.description: Use one game mechanic. name: a mechanic named callable in the latest SYLVIA_GM_CALLABLE_TOOLS record. arguments: an object of the shape its SYLVIA_GM_TOOL_DEFINITIONS entry shows.

function.name: tool_000000000007_start_group_combat_encounter
function.description:
Roll Initiative once for every living creature taking part in a group encounter. Supply all player characters, GM-controlled companions, and hostiles that are present when combat starts. The engine owns the resulting order; never omit a present companion merely to fit the two-creature encounter operation.
Coordinate combat requires a saved spatial scene. For the first encounter, supply one scene in combat_scenes using the spatial_scene format 1 content definition: format=1; map with id, revision, bounds.min/max (three coordinates), grid.cell_size/unit='ft'/origin (two coordinates), and layers (id/min_elevation/max_elevation); entities, geometry, zones and terrain arrays. Each combatant needs exactly one active creature body: id, map_id, position (three coordinates), footprint (box.half_extents or circle.radius), height, facing (two coordinates), active, movement, visibility, and metadata with participant_ref equal to its saved actor ID, creature_type, plane and lighting. Choose physical positions and body dimensions from the encounter fiction; do not invent a target-distance substitute. Include known blockers and terrain. Declare metadata.player.label/kind only on bodies and geometry the player knows. 
Coordinate combat uses the saved spatial scene. Supply one combat_scenes entry when admitting a later roster or an actual new arena. Omit it to reuse the scene. For the same map ID, keep the existing bounds, grid and layers: all saved bodies, objects, blockers, zones and terrain remain authoritative; supplied rows with existing IDs do not edit or relocate them. New IDs add genuinely present scene facts. For a new map ID, explicitly place every accompanying saved body/object by its exact ID. Existing dimensions, activity and mechanic metadata are retained; only actual destination position, facing, plane and ambient lighting are admitted. Include active summons, carried/worn objects, and a live Mage Hand with its cargo and caster. Arena replacement is unavailable while an anchored object, wall panel including permanent Stone, retained coordinate area/terrain or anchored light needs its current scene. Those effects are preserved and the operation clearly rejects before initiative; do not remove them or substitute a different map ID to bypass this limit. Exploration does not require map movement.

uncanny_metabolism_users.description: Monk combatants choosing Uncanny Metabolism when Initiative is rolled: regain all Focus and heal Monk level plus the Martial Arts die, once per Long Rest. Leave empty to decline; eligible level-15 Monks then receive Perfect Focus automatically.

player_intent_after_preparation.description: Declare what remains of the exact current player request after this preparation succeeds. Use unresolved_action if an attack or other action was declared and still needs resolution; omission has that same meaning. Use await_player_choice only when the request ends at preparation, such as establishing Initiative before the player chooses an action. Never use it to abandon an already-declared action or invent the player's next choice. This is provider-only control, not a Ruleset or Campaign State field.

function.name: tool_000000000017_ability_check
function.description: Resolve an identified character's ability check without a skill, using a tool, or using a different ability with a skill when the situation warrants it. Name one of the six abilities and any applicable skill/tool. The engine derives ability and ordinary proficiency modifiers from the saved character. Relevant skill and tool proficiency together grant Advantage, never a second proficiency bonus. Use only for uncertain outcomes that matter. Use dedicated Hide, Search, Study, Influence or combat operations when their rules apply. This operation does not infer class features such as Expertise; adjudicate their documented effects explicitly.

function.name: tool_000000000022_start_combat_encounter_entities
function.description:
Roll Initiative and establish an encounter between two canonical creature states. When combat is inactive and the player declares a hostile weapon attack against a known present creature, including a companion, you MUST call this operation before any player-facing prose and before resolving the attack, then follow the freshly exposed combat lifecycle and weapon-attack operations. Do not decide in prose that the attack misses, is deflected, or is de-escalated. Do not restate the scene or ask what the player does instead. Do not substitute an Athletics or other skill check for the attack.
Coordinate combat requires a saved spatial scene. For the first encounter, supply one scene in combat_scenes using the spatial_scene format 1 content definition: format=1; map with id, revision, bounds.min/max (three coordinates), grid.cell_size/unit='ft'/origin (two coordinates), and layers (id/min_elevation/max_elevation); entities, geometry, zones and terrain arrays. Each combatant needs exactly one active creature body: id, map_id, position (three coordinates), footprint (box.half_extents or circle.radius), height, facing (two coordinates), active, movement, visibility, and metadata with participant_ref equal to its saved actor ID, creature_type, plane and lighting. Choose physical positions and body dimensions from the encounter fiction; do not invent a target-distance substitute. Include known blockers and terrain. Declare metadata.player.label/kind only on bodies and geometry the player knows. 
Coordinate combat uses the saved spatial scene. Supply one combat_scenes entry when admitting a later roster or an actual new arena. Omit it to reuse the scene. For the same map ID, keep the existing bounds, grid and layers: all saved bodies, objects, blockers, zones and terrain remain authoritative; supplied rows with existing IDs do not edit or relocate them. New IDs add genuinely present scene facts. For a new map ID, explicitly place every accompanying saved body/object by its exact ID. Existing dimensions, activity and mechanic metadata are retained; only actual destination position, facing, plane and ambient lighting are admitted. Include active summons, carried/worn objects, and a live Mage Hand with its cargo and caster. Arena replacement is unavailable while an anchored object, wall panel including permanent Stone, retained coordinate area/terrain or anchored light needs its current scene. Those effects are preserved and the operation clearly rejects before initiative; do not remove them or substitute a different map ID to bypass this limit. Exploration does not require map movement.

function.description:

Omitted or false means hidden on the combat map. This fact does not reveal its caster or any creature, authorize movement, or change spell mechanics. For Misty Step outside combat, supply exactly one established destination fact record: its named place, actual current_plane and destination plane, horizontal_distance_feet, signed elevation_change_feet (negative means downward), visible and unoccupied. Do not invent these facts; the destination must be on the current plane and within the original 30-foot straight-line range, including either upward or downward elevation. Combat ignores this record and uses travel_destination and the saved scene.
Outside combat, Find Steed and Summon Dragon use established fictional placement. Supply created_actor_placement (a short established location), created_actor_distance in feet, created_actor_space_unoccupied=true and created_actor_clear_path=true. Summon Dragon also requires created_actor_space_visible=true; Find Steed does not. These facts do not create coordinates. The paid creature keeps its exact saved ID and source statistics. At later combat entry, explicitly include its same ID, printed Large box footprint, actual height/position/plane/ambient lighting and source metadata in combat_scenes. Combat movement, mounting and attacks use that admitted body. Exploration Steed abilities and mounting use current fiction as described by their tools. Combat casting still uses the authoritative scene and its actual placement/sight checks.
Outside combat, when this spell heals a caster with an active Otherworldly Steed, first call establish_srd_lite_steed_healing_proximity with that exact caster and Steed, their current established nearest separation in feet, and whether they currently share a plane. This fact authorizes one healing qualification at the current lasting tick; establish it immediately before the healing event. Birth placement is never current proximity. Combat Life Bond always measures the admitted actual bodies. Outside combat, Mage Hand uses current fictional placement, nearest caster separation and actual clear-path/contact facts, including its cargo and shared plane. No combat turn or map is required. A later Magic action advances ordinary time by one round; the hand moves at most 30 feet and vanishes beyond 30 feet from its caster. Outside combat, Thaumaturgy uses current established origin_distance, origin_has_clear_path and minor_same_plane facts for remote wonders, flames and doors/windows, even when an old combat map is saved. Use the exact admitted minor_object_id and existing subject/access/flame facts. Altered Eyes and Booming Voice affect the actual caster. No exploration coordinates are inferred.
For the offered spell bodies, Stone/Fire walls, Aura of Life and magical light, set known_spell_effect=true only for this cast's effect or created body whose presence and placement the player knows from a visible cast or an established current fact. It presents that effect, never a hidden caster, target, scouting eye or unrelated source. Omitted/false keeps private effects private. Range extents do not establish recipients, illumination, damage or safe movement.

function.name: tool_000000000001_update_campaign_file
function.description: Use character_updates for Ruleset-declared ordinary inventory/currency bookkeeping. Read the participant campaign reference for current fields, exact schema and revision first; submit complete replacement field values preserving unrelated holdings. Narrative attributes/facts alone never change equipment or money. Send related character changes and transaction facts together; rejection saves neither. Do not narrate success before acceptance or call failure a stale panel. Combat outcomes require their mechanics. When inventory_updates is offered, it is the active fallback for this campaign. Read campaign_state path inventory for its current holdings and revision; establish owner/holder entities in the same call when needed. Use holdings to establish or correct counts and transfers to move existing quantities. Loans, storage and returns preserve ownership; only explicit gifts/sales change it. Never infer currency exchange rates or use the fallback to bypass a Ruleset rejection. Update your durable Campaign File to the complete decided post-action truth in effect when control returns to the player. If Sylvia is holding a player-facing response, review it against that truth before committing. Store every lasting truth the response establishes or changes, including newly introduced people, places, objects, clues, relationships, promises, knowledge, scene state, and Plan Progress together in one call. Record the GM-owned outcome, not a summary of the player's request and not transient atmosphere. Use Ruleset tools for mechanics. The whole update is validated and committed together before the player sees the response. Any player-facing response and this disposition must describe the same post-action truth. Sylvia releases a settled response only after this call succeeds; it must not advance beyond or contradict the admitted durable state. Set state_change to 'unchanged' and omit all state collections only when the response changes no durable Campaign File truth; that records an unchanged decision without creating a database revision. An unchanged assessment asserts that location, scene, time, physical positions, player or NPC decisions, knowledge, relationships, people, places, objects, reveals, and Plan status are all exactly unchanged from the supplied pre-action State. An unsuccessful outcome can still change location, time, knowledge, or scene facts; record those consequences even when the player's goal remains unmet. Restating supplied Campaign State is not a change. Omit unchanged collections; an included collection must contain at least one change. Use only the declared top-level fields; do not invent convenience keys.

state_change.description: After you compare the complete response with pre-action Campaign State, declare whether any durable truth changed. Use 'changed' when any supplied collection records new post-action truth, otherwise use 'unchanged'.

state_change_summary.description: Brief private accounting of what durably changed, or why the response leaves Campaign State exactly unchanged. This assessment is audited but is not itself stored as campaign truth. Maximum 1000 characters, including spaces and newlines. Aim for one or two short sentences well below the maximum; put full facts in their own records instead of repeating them here.

entity_id.description: Stable campaign identity. Reuse it when the same person, place, creature, or object changes later.

entity_kind.description: Plain entity kind, such as person, place, creature, or object.

name.description: Current name, 1-300 characters, appropriate to this record's visibility. An unrevealed true name from Plan or Setting preparation belongs in a gm_private entity record, not a player_known one.

attributes.description: Current campaign-specific facts, such as location, condition, allegiance, or status. Include the complete current values that should remain true. For a player character, never infer posture, alertness, equipment use, or another action from inventory alone.

visibility.description: Knowledge boundary for the entire entity record, including its name and attributes. Use player_known only when every included detail has been established for the player; otherwise use gm_private.

known_by.description: Exact identities that have actually learned this entity state in the fiction. Do not include the player merely because the GM knows it or plans a future reveal.

source_ref.description: Optional admitted Setting or participant source path for this identity. Omit when there is no admitted source; never send an empty string.

entities.description: Every change of this kind established by the current GM response. Omit this collection when none changed.

fact_id.description: A stable identifier for this lasting campaign fact. Reuse it when a plan is completed, an obligation fulfilled, or this truth corrected. Write the complete current truth, including the outcome; earlier versions remain in history. If separate records already describe the old plan and its outcome, update the old plan record to say it is completed or superseded instead of leaving it as a current instruction.

category.description: The kind of lasting fact established by play.

text.description: The concise campaign-specific truth to remember (1-2000 characters). Keep separate lasting facts in separate records.

visibility.description: Knowledge boundary for the entire fact as written. Use player_known only when released play, player-authored text, or prior player-known Campaign State establishes every detail; otherwise use gm_private.

known_by.description: Exact identities that have actually learned this truth in the fiction. Do not include the player merely because the GM knows it or plans a future reveal.

subjects.description: Optional stable entity identifiers this fact is about.

facts.description: Every change of this kind established by the current GM response. Omit this collection when none changed.

summary.description: The concise current scene situation established by play (1-2000 characters). Never add a player action or equipment posture that player text, the participant artifact, or existing Campaign State did not establish.

act_id.description: Optional Campaign Plan preparation item associated with what play reached.

scenes.description: Every change of this kind established by the current GM response. Omit this collection when none changed.

secret_id.description: An established secret currently eligible to be revealed.

audience.description: Exact identities that learned the secret in play.

reveals.description: Every change of this kind established by the current GM response. Omit this collection when none changed.

plan_item_id.description: Exact private Campaign Plan item identity from the current choices record.

progress_status.description: What play has actually done with this prepared item, never what the Plan hoped would happen. 'Introduced' means the GM made it available while the player's response remains unresolved; 'engaged' requires a player choice that interacts with it; 'deferred' means the player clearly declined, avoided, or left the introduced material behind. Deferred material remains possible but is not a current obligation. 'Resolved' means play has met all authored completion conditions and the closing event, including an explicitly allowed failure outcome. An act requires all of its linked objectives; side work cannot replace them. 'Retired' means play has made the item inapplicable, not that the act was completed. For ending:<id>, read the final act/structured/ending and resolve only after required acts/objectives and the selected immediate aftermath. This opens the player's continue/finish card; leave the after-story for their explicit Finish choice. Plan Progress is a bookmark, not a turn log: omit it when the status and practical meaning have not changed.

progress_summary.description: Short private reason, 1-2000 characters, grounded only in what play established. Describe what was offered or changed, and record an express player choice when it changes the status. Refresh a superseded summary when the outcome, evidence, or remaining obligation changes even if the status stays engaged. Do not rewrite an existing summary merely to mention the current turn when its status and practical meaning are unchanged. Otherwise leave the player's response unresolved. Never infer the player's interest, intent, acceptance, route, or next action. Do not describe the player as weighing, considering, interested in, or drawn to an option unless player text establishes it; use neutral no-choice-yet wording instead.

plan_progress.description: Every change of this kind established by the current GM response. Omit this collection when none changed.

character_updates.description: Every change of this kind established by the current GM response. Omit this collection when none changed.

text.description: Scene description, actions and speech attribution. Keep NPC spoken words in separate npc_utterance blocks.

speaker_id.description: Exact current Campaign Entity or visible non-player participant ID, or an entity_id this same update records in entities. Record a named NPC as an entity and use its ID. Use anonymous only for a speaker without an ID.

speaker_name.description: With speaker_id anonymous: the name or short description the player knows this speaker by, as the narration calls them. It labels the speech box.

spoken_words.description: Only the words this NPC says aloud, without enclosing quotation marks. No actions, gestures, speaker names or 'she says' attribution. End this utterance when narration interrupts, then resume speech in a new npc_utterance block, even for the same speaker.

revised_player_facing_response.description: One complete ordered response. Put scene prose in narration blocks, each NPC's spoken words only in npc_utterance.spoken_words, and any OOC reply in a separate ooc block. NPC dialogue uses an exact current Campaign Entity or visible non-player participant speaker_id, an entity_id this same update records, or the anonymous sentinel with a speaker_name. Use one narration block for a response without dialogue. Sylvia holds the response until this Campaign File disposition succeeds. The collections and response must describe the same post-action truth. If an earlier response is already held, return its complete corrected replacement or an exact copy when it is already right; never return an edit note.

For Misty Step outside combat, supply exactly one established destination fact record: its named place, actual current_plane and destination plane, horizontal_distance_feet, signed elevation_change_feet (negative means downward), visible and unoccupied. For the offered spell bodies, Stone/Fire walls, Aura of Life and magical light, set known_spell_effect=true only for this cast's effect or created body whose presence and placement the player knows from a visible cast or an established current fact. function.name: tool_00000000004f_prepare_srd_creature
function.description: Prepare one new NPC or monster from a read Plan/Setting stat block, or an explicitly recorded GM adjudication, before starting combat. This creates authoritative creature state; narrative characters do not create it. Use one stable ID per individual. Existing identities and Player Characters/Companions are rejected without resetting them. Copy source defenses and any known save modifiers. This does not automate unencoded traits or an entire stat block. After success, start the intended encounter with this ID and the admitted party IDs before narrating its result. For spellcasters, copy the listed spells, casting statistics and per-day uses from the source. Zero uses_per_day means at will. Do not infer spell slots or cantrip scaling from Challenge Rating.

armor_class.description: AC from the source or explicit GM adjudication.

cantrip_scaling_level.description: Default 1. Supply another level only when the stat block explicitly grants scaled cantrips; never substitute Challenge Rating.

constitution_save.description: Optional signed constitution saving-throw modifier. Supply the source value or explicitly adjudicate it; omission does not establish a zero modifier.

creature_type.description: Creature type from the selected stat block. Omit when unknown; type-qualified spell effects cannot infer it.

damage_immunities.description: Copy all damage immunities from the source; an omitted list means none.

damage_resistances.description: Copy all damage resistances from the source; an omitted list means none.

damage_vulnerabilities.description: Copy all damage vulnerabilities from the source; an omitted list means none.

dexterity_save.description: Optional signed dexterity saving-throw modifier. Supply the source value or explicitly adjudicate it; omission does not establish a zero modifier.

Record base speeds before armor, AC without worn gear (including natural defenses), Strength/Dexterity, armor training, and zero or one carried item in armor/shield. Supplied final AC and walking Speed must agree. Omit only when gear changes are not needed.

flying_speed.description: Copy actual native Flying Speed from the source; zero if none.

hit_points.description: Current and maximum HP for this newly introduced, unwounded creature. Never prepare an existing wounded creature again.

initiative_modifier.description: Signed Initiative modifier from the source or explicit GM adjudication.

intelligence_save.description: Optional signed intelligence saving-throw modifier. Supply the source value or explicitly adjudicate it; omission does not establish a zero modifier.

saving_throw_proficiencies.description: Copy the explicit complete proficiency list from the source. Omission leaves training unknown; an empty list explicitly records none.

size_rank.description: Size from the source or recorded adjudication: Tiny 0, Small 1, Medium 2, Large 3, Huge 4, Gargantuan 5.

skill_checks.description: Actual total NPC skill-check modifiers from the selected stat block. For an unlisted skill use its actual ability modifier. Omitted skills remain unknown; never guess them from saving throws.

function.name: tool_000000000002_read_campaign_reference
function.description: READ-ONLY: retrieve current Campaign State or one additional available Plan, Setting, Ruleset, or Character File. A participant reference returns that admitted character's authored summary and structured baseline when available. This tool cannot update, write, save, or commit Campaign File state. Campaign State is current truth; Plan and Setting material are preparation and defaults. Read for a concrete missing fact that changes present adjudication, or consult Plan preparation when choosing a new situation, assessing objective completion, or closing an episode. Read the smallest relevant item, not to decorate or expand narration. Retrieved detail remains private unless the current action and vantage reveal it. Do not reread Plan or Setting material already projected into the current request. An ID, title or reference path does not include the source contents. For an engine-owned structured input format, read source engine_format, path spatial_scene before constructing a combat scene; it returns the installed schema, example and requirements.

path.description: For campaign_state prefer a stable Campaign File record ID from search_campaign_knowledge. 'current' reads all state and may exceed the byte bound in a mature campaign. For campaign_plan use 'structured' for the whole Plan, 'structured/structure/<act-id>' for one act, 'structured/objectives/<objective-id>' for one objective and its completion conditions, or 'readable'. For a longer readable Plan use 'readable/page/0' and follow the returned next_path; each page is bounded. For participant use its exact participant ID to retrieve that Character File. For campaign_setting or ruleset use an exact admitted package path. Append '#heading-slug' to read one Markdown section without reading the rest of its file. Large UTF-8 files return bounded '#text/<character-offset>' excerpts. Follow next_path or search_campaign_knowledge for a relevant excerpt. For engine_format use spatial_scene (the installed scene schema and example).

function.name: tool_0000000000aa_spend_combat_movement
function.description: Spend a positive distance of normal or Difficult Terrain movement before or after the turn's action. Use this only when the active creature actually moves a declared distance; never use it to end a turn or discard unused movement. Call end_combat_turn for that instead. For a character’s unobstructed jump, choose long_jump or high_jump and declare the actual running start; the engine derives reach and spends each foot once. For long_jump, difficult_terrain means the landing requires its DC 10 Acrobatics check. Obstacle-clearance rulings are separate. For a Monk of level 9 or higher wearing no armor and wielding no Shield, choose vertical_surface or liquid_surface for Acrobatic Movement. Do not narrate success before acceptance or call failure a stale panel. Combat outcomes require their mechanics. When inventory_updates is offered, it is the active fallback for this campaign. Read campaign_state path inventory for its current holdings and revision; establish owner/holder entities in the same call when needed. Use holdings to establish or correct counts and transfers to move existing quantities. Loans, storage and returns preserve ownership; only explicit gifts/sales change it. Never infer currency exchange rates or use the fallback to bypass a Ruleset rejection. Update your durable Campaign File to the complete decided post-action truth in effect when control returns to the player. If Sylvia is holding a player-facing response, review it against that truth before committing. Store every lasting truth the response establishes or changes, including newly introduced people, places, objects, clues, relationships, promises, knowledge, scene state, and Plan Progress together in one call. Record the GM-owned outcome, not a summary of the player's request and not transient atmosphere. Use Ruleset tools for mechanics. The whole update is validated and committed together before the player sees the response. Any player-facing response and this disposition must describe the same post-action truth. Sylvia releases a settled response only after this call succeeds; it must not advance beyond or contradict the admitted durable state. Set state_change to 'unchanged' and omit all state collections only when the response changes no durable Campaign File truth; that records an unchanged decision without creating a database revision. An unchanged assessment asserts that location, scene, time, physical positions, player or NPC decisions, knowledge, relationships, people, places, objects, reveals, and Plan status are all exactly unchanged from the supplied pre-action State. An unsuccessful outcome can still change location, time, knowledge, or scene facts; record those consequences even when the player's goal remains unmet. Restating supplied Campaign State is not a change. Omit unchanged collections; an included collection must contain at least one change. Use only the declared top-level fields; do not invent convenience keys.

state_change.description: After you compare the complete response with pre-action Campaign State, declare whether any durable truth changed. Use 'changed' when any supplied collection records new post-action truth, otherwise use 'unchanged'.

state_change_summary.description: Brief private accounting of what durably changed, or why the response leaves Campaign State exactly unchanged. This assessment is audited but is not itself stored as campaign truth. Maximum 1000 characters, including spaces and newlines. Aim for one or two short sentences well below the maximum; put full facts in their own records instead of repeating them here.

Deferred material remains possible but is not a current obligation. 'Resolved' means play has met all authored completion conditions and the closing event, including an explicitly allowed failure outcome. An act requires all of its linked objectives; side work cannot replace them. 'Retired' means play has made the item inapplicable, not that the act was completed. Do not rewrite an existing summary merely to mention the current turn when its status and practical meaning are unchanged. Otherwise leave the player's response unresolved. function.name: start_group_combat_encounter
function.description:
Roll Initiative once for every living creature taking part in a group encounter. Supply all player characters, GM-controlled companions, and hostiles that are present when combat starts. The engine owns the resulting order; never omit a present companion merely to fit the two-creature encounter operation.
Coordinate combat requires a saved spatial scene. For the first encounter, supply one scene in combat_scenes using the spatial_scene format 1 content definition: format=1; map with id, revision, bounds.min/max (three coordinates), grid.cell_size/unit='ft'/origin (two coordinates), and layers (id/min_elevation/max_elevation); entities, geometry, zones and terrain arrays. Each combatant needs exactly one active creature body: id, map_id, position (three coordinates), footprint (box.half_extents or circle.radius), height, facing (two coordinates), active, movement, visibility, and metadata with participant_ref equal to its saved actor ID, creature_type, plane and lighting. Choose physical positions and body dimensions from the encounter fiction; do not invent a target-distance substitute. Include known blockers and terrain. Declare metadata.player.label/kind only on bodies and geometry the player knows. 
Coordinate combat uses the saved spatial scene. Supply one combat_scenes entry when admitting a later roster or an actual new arena. Omit it to reuse the scene. For the same map ID, keep the existing bounds, grid and layers: all saved bodies, objects, blockers, zones and terrain remain authoritative; supplied rows with existing IDs do not edit or relocate them. New IDs add genuinely present scene facts. For a new map ID, explicitly place every accompanying saved body/object by its exact ID. Existing dimensions, activity and mechanic metadata are retained; only actual destination position, facing, plane and ambient lighting are admitted. Include active summons, carried/worn objects, and a live Mage Hand with its cargo and caster. Arena replacement is unavailable while an anchored object, wall panel including permanent Stone, retained coordinate area/terrain or anchored light needs its current scene. Those effects are preserved and the operation clearly rejects before initiative; do not remove them or substitute a different map ID to bypass this limit. Exploration does not require map movement.

function.name: cast_spell_outside_combat
function.description:
Cast one of the package's executable prepared spells using its admitted spell definition and reusable resolution family.
For Web, Cloud of Daggers, Insect Plague, Stinking Cloud, Fog Cloud, Sleet Storm or Zone of Truth, set known_area=true only when the player knows the committed spell area from observing the cast or another established fact. Omitted or false means hidden on the combat map. This fact does not reveal its caster or any creature, authorize movement, or change spell mechanics. For Misty Step outside combat, supply exactly one established destination fact record: its named place, actual current_plane and destination plane, horizontal_distance_feet, signed elevation_change_feet (negative means downward), visible and unoccupied. Do not invent these facts; the destination must be on the current plane and within the original 30-foot straight-line range, including either upward or downward elevation. Combat ignores this record and uses travel_destination and the saved scene.
Outside combat, Find Steed and Summon Dragon use established fictional placement. Supply created_actor_placement (a short established location), created_actor_distance in feet, created_actor_space_unoccupied=true and created_actor_clear_path=true. Summon Dragon also requires created_actor_space_visible=true; Find Steed does not. These facts do not create coordinates. The paid creature keeps its exact saved ID and source statistics. At later combat entry, explicitly include its same ID, printed Large box footprint, actual height/position/plane/ambient lighting and source metadata in combat_scenes. Combat movement, mounting and attacks use that admitted body. Exploration Steed abilities and mounting use current fiction as described by their tools. Combat casting still uses the authoritative scene and its actual placement/sight checks.
Outside combat, when this spell heals a caster with an active Otherworldly Steed, first call establish_srd_lite_steed_healing_proximity with that exact caster and Steed, their current established nearest separation in feet, and whether they currently share a plane. This fact authorizes one healing qualification at the current lasting tick; establish it immediately before the healing event. Birth placement is never current proximity. Combat Life Bond always measures the admitted actual bodies. Outside combat, Mage Hand uses current fictional placement, nearest caster separation and actual clear-path/contact facts, including its cargo and shared plane. No combat turn or map is required. A later Magic action advances ordinary time by one round; the hand moves at most 30 feet and vanishes beyond 30 feet from its caster. Outside combat, Thaumaturgy uses current established origin_distance, origin_has_clear_path and minor_same_plane facts for remote wonders, flames and doors/windows, even when an old combat map is saved. Use the exact admitted minor_object_id and existing subject/access/flame facts. Altered Eyes and Booming Voice affect the actual caster. No exploration coordinates are inferred.
For the offered spell bodies, Stone/Fire walls, Aura of Life and magical light, set known_spell_effect=true only for this cast's effect or created body whose presence and placement the player knows from a visible cast or an established current fact. It presents that effect, never a hidden caster, target, scouting eye or unrelated source. Omitted/false keeps private effects private. Range extents do not establish recipients, illumination, damage or safe movement.

function.name: begin_srd_spell_action
function.description:
In combat, begin a source-validated casting action before its spell resolves. Outside combat, cast with cast_spell_outside_combat instead.
For Web, Cloud of Daggers, Insect Plague, Stinking Cloud, Fog Cloud, Sleet Storm or Zone of Truth, set known_area=true only when the player knows the committed spell area from observing the cast or another established fact. Omitted or false means hidden on the combat map. This fact does not reveal its caster or any creature, authorize movement, or change spell mechanics. In combat, Flame Strike requires environment_origin as its chosen Cylinder point; saved positions determine recipients, range and cover. In combat, Fear uses the saved body facing or instant_area_direction/apex for its Cone; Sleep chooses environment_origin for its Sphere. Saved positions determine actual recipients, range, plane and clear paths. For Misty Step outside combat, supply exactly one established destination fact record: its named place, actual current_plane and destination plane, horizontal_distance_feet, signed elevation_change_feet (negative means downward), visible and unoccupied. Do not invent these facts; the destination must be on the current plane and within the original 30-foot straight-line range, including either upward or downward elevation. Combat ignores this record and uses travel_destination and the saved scene.
Outside combat, Find Steed and Summon Dragon use established fictional placement. Supply created_actor_placement (a short established location), created_actor_distance in feet, created_actor_space_unoccupied=true and created_actor_clear_path=true. Summon Dragon also requires created_actor_space_visible=true; Find Steed does not. These facts do not create coordinates. The paid creature keeps its exact saved ID and source statistics. At later combat entry, explicitly include its same ID, printed Large box footprint, actual height/position/plane/ambient lighting and source metadata in combat_scenes. Combat movement, mounting and attacks use that admitted body. Exploration Steed abilities and mounting use current fiction as described by their tools. Combat casting still uses the authoritative scene and its actual placement/sight checks.
Outside combat, when this spell heals a caster with an active Otherworldly Steed, first call establish_srd_lite_steed_healing_proximity with that exact caster and Steed, their current established nearest separation in feet, and whether they currently share a plane. This fact authorizes one healing qualification at the current lasting tick; establish it immediately before the healing event. Birth placement is never current proximity. Combat Life Bond always measures the admitted actual bodies. Outside combat, Mage Hand uses current fictional placement, nearest caster separation and actual clear-path/contact facts, including its cargo and shared plane. No combat turn or map is required. A later Magic action advances ordinary time by one round; the hand moves at most 30 feet and vanishes beyond 30 feet from its caster. Outside combat, Thaumaturgy uses current established origin_distance, origin_has_clear_path and minor_same_plane facts for remote wonders, flames and doors/windows, even when an old combat map is saved. Use the exact admitted minor_object_id and existing subject/access/flame facts. Altered Eyes and Booming Voice affect the actual caster. No exploration coordinates are inferred. In combat, known_area=true also displays a qualified pending area while its casting reaction window is open. Set it only when the player knows the actual chosen area, including any relocated origin. The preview does not reveal creatures, determine affected targets, spend a slot, or resolve the spell. Cone and Line displays show their exact XY footprint, clipped at map bounds; height still affects actual recipients.
For the offered spell bodies, Stone/Fire walls, Aura of Life and magical light, set known_spell_effect=true only for this cast's effect or created body whose presence and placement the player knows from a visible cast or an established current fact. It presents that effect, never a hidden caster, target, scouting eye or unrelated source. Omitted/false keeps private effects private. Range extents do not establish recipients, illumination, damage or safe movement.

function.name: prepare_srd_creature
function.description: Prepare one new NPC or monster from a read Plan/Setting stat block, or an explicitly recorded GM adjudication, before starting combat. This creates authoritative creature state; narrative characters do not create it. Use one stable ID per individual. Existing identities and Player Characters/Companions are rejected without resetting them. Copy source defenses and any known save modifiers. This does not automate unencoded traits or an entire stat block. After success, start the intended encounter with this ID and the admitted party IDs before narrating its result. For spellcasters, copy the listed spells, casting statistics and per-day uses from the source. Zero uses_per_day means at will. Do not infer spell slots or cantrip scaling from Challenge Rating.

function.name: spend_combat_movement
function.description: Spend a positive distance of normal or Difficult Terrain movement before or after the turn's action. Use this only when the active creature actually moves a declared distance; never use it to end a turn or discard unused movement. Call end_combat_turn for that instead. For a character’s unobstructed jump, choose long_jump or high_jump and declare the actual running start; the engine derives reach and spends each foot once. For long_jump, difficult_terrain means the landing requires its DC 10 Acrobatics check. Obstacle-clearance rulings are separate. For a Monk of level 9 or higher wearing no armor and wielding no Shield, choose vertical_surface or liquid_surface for Acrobatic Movement. This permits traversal only during this movement on the creature's turn; it does not grant flight, hovering, or the ability to remain unsupported after movement ends. The GM establishes the surface and endpoint from the scene. Active mobility spells also permit fly, climb, ceiling, liquid_surface, or spell_jump. Fly grants 60-foot flight and hovering; end_in_air records whether the creature remains aloft. Spider Climb uses current Speed on surfaces and ceilings with free hands. Jump spends 10 feet once per turn to jump up to 30 feet. Water Walk treats liquid as harmless solid ground while heat remains a separate hazard; use its transition action to enter it.

function.description: READ-ONLY: retrieve current Campaign State or one additional available Plan, Setting, Ruleset, or Character File. A participant reference returns that admitted character's authored summary and structured baseline when available. This tool cannot update, write, save, or commit Campaign File state. Campaign State is current truth; Plan and Setting material are preparation and defaults. Read for a concrete missing fact that changes present adjudication, or consult Plan preparation when choosing a new situation, assessing objective completion, or closing an episode. Read the smallest relevant item, not to decorate or expand narration. Retrieved detail remains private unless the current action and vantage reveal it. Do not reread Plan or Setting material already projected into the current request. An ID, title or reference path does not include the source contents. For an engine-owned structured input format, read source engine_format, path spatial_scene before constructing a combat scene; it returns the installed schema, example and requirements.

path.description: For campaign_state prefer a stable Campaign File record ID from search_campaign_knowledge. 'current' reads all state and may exceed the byte bound in a mature campaign. For campaign_plan use 'structured' for the whole Plan, 'structured/structure/<act-id>' for one act, 'structured/objectives/<objective-id>' for one objective and its completion conditions, or 'readable'. For a longer readable Plan use 'readable/page/0' and follow the returned next_path; each page is bounded. For participant use its exact participant ID to retrieve that Character File. For campaign_setting or ruleset use an exact admitted package path. Append '#heading-slug' to read one Markdown section without reading the rest of its file. Large UTF-8 files return bounded '#text/<character-offset>' excerpts. Follow next_path or search_campaign_knowledge for a relevant excerpt. For engine_format use spatial_scene (the installed scene schema and example).

function.description: Use character_updates for Ruleset-declared ordinary inventory/currency bookkeeping. Read the participant campaign reference for current fields, exact schema and revision first; submit complete replacement field values preserving unrelated holdings. Narrative attributes/facts alone never change equipment or money. Send related character changes and transaction facts together; rejection saves neither. Do not narrate success before acceptance or call failure a stale panel. Combat outcomes require their mechanics. When inventory_updates is offered, it is the active fallback for this campaign. Read campaign_state path inventory for its current holdings and revision; establish owner/holder entities in the same call when needed. Use holdings to establish or correct counts and transfers to move existing quantities. Loans, storage and returns preserve ownership; only explicit gifts/sales change it. Never infer currency exchange rates or use the fallback to bypass a Ruleset rejection. Update your durable Campaign File to the complete decided post-action truth in effect when control returns to the player. If Sylvia is holding a player-facing response, review it against that truth before committing. Store every lasting truth the response establishes or changes, including newly introduced people, places, objects, clues, relationships, promises, knowledge, scene state, and Plan Progress together in one call. Record the GM-owned outcome, not a summary of the player's request and not transient atmosphere. Use Ruleset tools for mechanics. The whole update is validated and committed together before the player sees the response. Any player-facing response and this disposition must describe the same post-action truth. Sylvia releases a settled response only after this call succeeds; it must not advance beyond or contradict the admitted durable state. Set state_change to 'unchanged' and omit all state collections only when the response changes no durable Campaign File truth; that records an unchanged decision without creating a database revision. An unchanged assessment asserts that location, scene, time, physical positions, player or NPC decisions, knowledge, relationships, people, places, objects, reveals, and Plan status are all exactly unchanged from the supplied pre-action State. An unsuccessful outcome can still change location, time, knowledge, or scene facts; record those consequences even when the player's goal remains unmet. Restating supplied Campaign State is not a change. Omit unchanged collections; an included collection must contain at least one change. Use only the declared top-level fields; do not invent convenience keys.

function.description:
Roll Initiative and establish an encounter between two canonical creature states. When combat is inactive and the player declares a hostile weapon attack against a known present creature, including a companion, you MUST call this operation before any player-facing prose and before resolving the attack, then follow the freshly exposed combat lifecycle and weapon-attack operations. Do not decide in prose that the attack misses, is deflected, or is de-escalated. Do not restate the scene or ask what the player does instead. Do not substitute an Athletics or other skill check for the attack.
Coordinate combat requires a saved spatial scene. For the first encounter, supply one scene in combat_scenes using the spatial_scene format 1 content definition: format=1; map with id, revision, bounds.min/max (three coordinates), grid.cell_size/unit='ft'/origin (two coordinates), and layers (id/min_elevation/max_elevation); entities, geometry, zones and terrain arrays. Each combatant needs exactly one active creature body: id, map_id, position (three coordinates), footprint (box.half_extents or circle.radius), height, facing (two coordinates), active, movement, visibility, and metadata with participant_ref equal to its saved actor ID, creature_type, plane and lighting. Choose physical positions and body dimensions from the encounter fiction; do not invent a target-distance substitute. Include known blockers and terrain. Declare metadata.player.label/kind only on bodies and geometry the player knows. 
Coordinate combat uses the saved spatial scene. Supply one combat_scenes entry when admitting a later roster or an actual new arena. Omit it to reuse the scene. For the same map ID, keep the existing bounds, grid and layers: all saved bodies, objects, blockers, zones and terrain remain authoritative; supplied rows with existing IDs do not edit or relocate them. New IDs add genuinely present scene facts. For a new map ID, explicitly place every accompanying saved body/object by its exact ID. Existing dimensions, activity and mechanic metadata are retained; only actual destination position, facing, plane and ambient lighting are admitted. Include active summons, carried/worn objects, and a live Mage Hand with its cargo and caster. Arena replacement is unavailable while an anchored object, wall panel including permanent Stone, retained coordinate area/terrain or anchored light needs its current scene. Those effects are preserved and the operation clearly rejects before initiative; do not remove them or substitute a different map ID to bypass this limit. Exploration does not require map movement.
function.name: tool_000000000022_start_combat_encounter_entities

Read for a concrete missing fact that changes present adjudication, or consult Plan preparation when choosing a new situation, assessing objective completion, or closing an episode. Read the smallest relevant item, not to decorate or expand narration. Retrieved detail remains private unless the current action and vantage reveal it. Do not reread Plan or Setting material already projected into the current request. An ID, title or reference path does not include the source contents. For an engine-owned structured input format, read source engine_format, path spatial_scene before constructing a combat scene; it returns the installed schema, example and requirements.
function.name: tool_000000000002_read_campaign_reference

path.description: For campaign_state prefer a stable Campaign File record ID from search_campaign_knowledge. 'current' reads all state and may exceed the byte bound in a mature campaign. For campaign_plan use 'structured' for the whole Plan, 'structured/structure/<act-id>' for one act, 'structured/objectives/<objective-id>' for one objective and its completion conditions, or 'readable'. For a longer readable Plan use 'readable/page/0' and follow the returned next_path; each page is bounded. For participant use its exact participant ID to retrieve that Character File. For campaign_setting or ruleset use an exact admitted package path. Append '#heading-slug' to read one Markdown section without reading the rest of its file. Large UTF-8 files return bounded '#text/<character-offset>' excerpts. Follow next_path or search_campaign_knowledge for a relevant excerpt. For engine_format use spatial_scene (the installed scene schema and example).

function.description: Use character_updates for Ruleset-declared ordinary inventory/currency bookkeeping. Read the participant campaign reference for current fields, exact schema and revision first; submit complete replacement field values preserving unrelated holdings. Narrative attributes/facts alone never change equipment or money. Send related character changes and transaction facts together; rejection saves neither. Do not narrate success before acceptance or call failure a stale panel. Combat outcomes require their mechanics. When inventory_updates is offered, it is the active fallback for this campaign. Read campaign_state path inventory for its current holdings and revision; establish owner/holder entities in the same call when needed. Use holdings to establish or correct counts and transfers to move existing quantities. Loans, storage and returns preserve ownership; only explicit gifts/sales change it. Never infer currency exchange rates or use the fallback to bypass a Ruleset rejection. Update your durable Campaign File to the complete decided post-action truth in effect when control returns to the player. If Sylvia is holding a player-facing response, review it against that truth before committing. Store every lasting truth the response establishes or changes, including newly introduced people, places, objects, clues, relationships, promises, knowledge, scene state, and Plan Progress together in one call. Record the GM-owned outcome, not a summary of the player's request and not transient atmosphere. Use Ruleset tools for mechanics. The whole update is validated and committed together before the player sees the response. Any player-facing response and this disposition must describe the same post-action truth. Sylvia releases a settled response only after this call succeeds; it must not advance beyond or contradict the admitted durable state. Set state_change to 'unchanged' and omit all state collections only when the response changes no durable Campaign File truth; that records an unchanged decision without creating a database revision. An unchanged assessment asserts that location, scene, time, physical positions, player or NPC decisions, knowledge, relationships, people, places, objects, reveals, and Plan status are all exactly unchanged from the supplied pre-action State. An unsuccessful outcome can still change location, time, knowledge, or scene facts; record those consequences even when the player's goal remains unmet. Restating supplied Campaign State is not a change. Omit unchanged collections; an included collection must contain at least one change. Use only the declared top-level fields; do not invent convenience keys.
function.name: tool_000000000001_update_campaign_file

character_updates.description: Every change of this kind established by the current GM response. Omit this collection when none changed.

entities.description: Every change of this kind established by the current GM response. Omit this collection when none changed.

attributes.description: Current campaign-specific facts, such as location, condition, allegiance, or status. Include the complete current values that should remain true. For a player character, never infer posture, alertness, equipment use, or another action from inventory alone.

entity_id.description: Stable campaign identity. Reuse it when the same person, place, creature, or object changes later.

entity_kind.description: Plain entity kind, such as person, place, creature, or object.

known_by.description: Exact identities that have actually learned this entity state in the fiction. Do not include the player merely because the GM knows it or plans a future reveal.

name.description: Current name, 1-300 characters, appropriate to this record's visibility. An unrevealed true name from Plan or Setting preparation belongs in a gm_private entity record, not a player_known one.

source_ref.description: Optional admitted Setting or participant source path for this identity. Omit when there is no admitted source; never send an empty string.

visibility.description: Knowledge boundary for the entire entity record, including its name and attributes. Use player_known only when every included detail has been established for the player; otherwise use gm_private.

facts.description: Every change of this kind established by the current GM response. Omit this collection when none changed.

category.description: The kind of lasting fact established by play.

fact_id.description: A stable identifier for this lasting campaign fact. Reuse it when a plan is completed, an obligation fulfilled, or this truth corrected. Write the complete current truth, including the outcome; earlier versions remain in history. If separate records already describe the old plan and its outcome, update the old plan record to say it is completed or superseded instead of leaving it as a current instruction.

known_by.description: Exact identities that have actually learned this truth in the fiction. Do not include the player merely because the GM knows it or plans a future reveal.

subjects.description: Optional stable entity identifiers this fact is about.

text.description: The concise campaign-specific truth to remember (1-2000 characters). Keep separate lasting facts in separate records.

visibility.description: Knowledge boundary for the entire fact as written. Use player_known only when released play, player-authored text, or prior player-known Campaign State establishes every detail; otherwise use gm_private.

plan_progress.description: Every change of this kind established by the current GM response. Omit this collection when none changed.

plan_item_id.description: Exact private Campaign Plan item identity from this enum.

progress_status.description: What play has actually done with this prepared item, never what the Plan hoped would happen. 'Introduced' means the GM made it available while the player's response remains unresolved; 'engaged' requires a player choice that interacts with it; 'deferred' means the player clearly declined, avoided, or left the introduced material behind. Deferred material remains possible but is not a current obligation. 'Resolved' means play has met all authored completion conditions and the closing event, including an explicitly allowed failure outcome. An act requires all of its linked objectives; side work cannot replace them. 'Retired' means play has made the item inapplicable, not that the act was completed. For ending:<id>, read the final act/structured/ending and resolve only after required acts/objectives and the selected immediate aftermath. This opens the player's continue/finish card; leave the after-story for their explicit Finish choice. Plan Progress is a bookmark, not a turn log: omit it when the status and practical meaning have not changed.

progress_summary.description: Short private reason, 1-2000 characters, grounded only in what play established. Describe what was offered or changed, and record an express player choice when it changes the status. Refresh a superseded summary when the outcome, evidence, or remaining obligation changes even if the status stays engaged. Do not rewrite an existing summary merely to mention the current turn when its status and practical meaning are unchanged. Otherwise leave the player's response unresolved. Never infer the player's interest, intent, acceptance, route, or next action. Do not describe the player as weighing, considering, interested in, or drawn to an option unless player text establishes it; use neutral no-choice-yet wording instead.

reveals.description: Every change of this kind established by the current GM response. Omit this collection when none changed.

audience.description: Exact identities that learned the secret in play.

secret_id.description: An established secret currently eligible to be revealed.

revised_player_facing_response.description: One complete ordered response. Put scene prose in narration blocks, each NPC's spoken words only in npc_utterance.spoken_words, and any OOC reply in a separate ooc block. NPC dialogue uses an exact current Campaign Entity or visible non-player participant speaker_id, an entity_id this same update records, or the anonymous sentinel with a speaker_name. Use one narration block for a response without dialogue. Sylvia holds the response until this Campaign File disposition succeeds. The collections and response must describe the same post-action truth. If an earlier response is already held, return its complete corrected replacement or an exact copy when it is already right; never return an edit note.

text.description: Scene description, actions and speech attribution. Keep NPC spoken words in separate npc_utterance blocks.

speaker_id.description: Exact current Campaign Entity or visible non-player participant ID, or an entity_id this same update records in entities. Record a named NPC as an entity and use its ID. Use anonymous only for a speaker without an ID.

speaker_name.description: With speaker_id anonymous: the name or short description the player knows this speaker by, as the narration calls them. It labels the speech box.

spoken_words.description: Only the words this NPC says aloud, without enclosing quotation marks. No actions, gestures, speaker names or 'she says' attribution. End this utterance when narration interrupts, then resume speech in a new npc_utterance block, even for the same speaker.

scenes.description: Every change of this kind established by the current GM response. Omit this collection when none changed.

act_id.description: Optional Campaign Plan preparation item associated with what play reached.

summary.description: The concise current scene situation established by play (1-2000 characters). Never add a player action or equipment posture that player text, the participant artifact, or existing Campaign State did not establish.

state_change.description: After you compare the complete response with pre-action Campaign State, declare whether any durable truth changed. Use 'changed' when any supplied collection records new post-action truth, otherwise use 'unchanged'.

state_change_summary.description: Brief private accounting of what durably changed, or why the response leaves Campaign State exactly unchanged. This assessment is audited but is not itself stored as campaign truth. Maximum 1000 characters, including spaces and newlines. Aim for one or two short sentences well below the maximum; put full facts in their own records instead of repeating them here.

Each selection_contract lists the exact required selection keys and current map_revision or graph_revision context values. Copy context values exactly and fill other keys from player intent. Only currently controlled, eligible actors may act. Stop on failed, stale or paused results; do not resume remaining intentions without a fresh player direction. Never implicitly End Turn, expand actor control, reroll or repeat a committed step. Narrate the committed outcomes together afterward through the ordinary Campaign File disposition.
